title: priv-iam-minimal-boundaries-module-for-vpc-deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Private (VPC) deployments currently rely on ad-hoc IAM role/policy templates maintained in multiple repos. This causes drift, inconsistent least-privilege boundaries, and manual effort during upgrades and audits. Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module that provides opinionated, minimal-privilege IAM/RBAC scaffolding for Redwood Private installs. The module should: generate roles and policies that follow principle-of-least-privilege, provide boundary/permission scoping patterns, support cross-account bootstrap and short-lived credentials, emit policy artifacts for audit, and include plan-time validation and runtime health checks to detect drift. It must be upgrade-friendly (schema migrations, safe default additions) and integrate with our Terraform registry and private deploy upgrade playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a minimal set of variables to define service identity, environment (dev/stage/prod), and optional affinity tags
Module produces IAM roles and attached managed or inline policies that adhere to documented least-privilege templates (compute, storage, networking, kms-access)
Module supports boundary policies (permissions boundary resource) and an optional prefix mode for tenant isolation

Plan-time validation includes: simulated permission checks (using policyonly or local simulator), warnings for wildcard actions/resources, and explicit list of required permissions for external operators
Upgrade path: module supports major/minor schema migrations with a clear migrate.sh helper and terraform migration guide in docs
Runtime health checks: a lightweight Lambda/agent (optional) can run hourly to assert role trust, policy attachments, and KMS key grants; it sends alerts to the infra-slo dashboard on deviation
Outputs: machine-readable policy JSON, role ARNs, a canonical responsibilities.md link, and an audit bundle (zip) for compliance teams
PR reviewed by Security and Infra leads and merged to registry with automated acceptance tests passing in the private deploy CI pipeline
tasks: RFC: propose module variable surface and least-privilege policy templates (owner: Rafael)
